cases.original_forecast: Acid/base recharge approximately restores the buffer ratio while sodium/chloride accumulate. Similar pH values need not imply identical conductivity or ionic strength.

criteria.criterion: The acetate pool remains constant through both cycles.
Final sodium and chloride increments equal the added strong acid/base budgets; conductivity is evaluated independently of pH recovery.

cases.original_forecast: One equivalent predominantly gives dihydrogen phosphate; two give hydrogen phosphate; a further half equivalent probes the third, high-pH region. These are different species distributions, not the same neutral salt.

criteria.criterion: Use solved phosphate species to interpret each pH, rather than assigning every neutralised salt pH seven.
Total phosphorus is 1 mmol in each vessel.

cases.original_forecast: The first stage preferentially retains magnesium hydroxide; the subsequent carbonate stage targets calcium in the first filtrate.

criteria.criterion: Quantify Ca and Mg in both solid fractions and final solution.
Do not call the separation quantitative without reporting cross-contamination.

cases.original_forecast: A modest chloride-containing rinse should reduce AgCl dissolution relative to a pure-water rinse, while both remove soluble impurities.

criteria.criterion: Compare Ag losses in the second filtrates v5 and v6.
Include silver already lost in the first filtration when calculating total recovery.

cases.original_forecast: An ideal concentration-ratio model predicts little change because both concentrations fall together; real activity and complexation corrections can produce a residual shift.

criteria.criterion: Reconstruct the prediction using solved Cu2+/Zn2+ activity ratios.
Do not label every nonzero voltage shift a failure of the Nernst relation.

reason.en: {name} stays as the metal: nothing dissolved here sits below it in the activity series. Its slow reaction with water itself — hydrogen over hours, a passivating hydroxide skin — is a rate this lab does not model

event.what: zinc stays as the metal: nothing dissolved here sits below it in the activity series. Its slow reaction with water itself — hydrogen over hours, a passivating hydroxide skin — is a rate this lab does not model

cases.original_forecast: AgCl precipitation lowers free Ag+ activity in one half-cell and can create a concentration-related voltage while both contain silver metal.

criteria.criterion: Require an AgCl phase and a lowered free-Ag+ activity in the treated half-cell.
Distinguish sign convention from the existence of a potential difference.

actual_events.why: both vessels present the same Ag | Ag+ electrode at the same activity: a cell of two identical half-cells reads 0 V
v2 has Ag but none of its ion in solution: a metal in water that does not contain its own ion has no defined potential here

cases.original_forecast: Reduction of available silver can draw further AgCl dissolution, yielding silver metal and dissolved zinc/chloride if the coupled phases are represented.

criteria.criterion: Require Ag metal formation with corresponding AgCl loss and Zn oxidation.
At most 0.4 mmol Ag originates from the introduced silver salt.

cases.original_forecast: Copper recovered from zinc displacement can reduce silver ions in a second stage. The interpretation depends on confirming that residual zinc is not the direct silver donor.

criteria.criterion: Inspect the first retained solid for residual Zn before attributing silver deposition to copper.
Track Cu oxidation and Ag reduction in a 1:2 electron ratio where copper is the donor.

cases.original_forecast: The 0.05 mmol copper inventory can accept only about 9.65 C for complete Cu(II)-to-Cu reduction. Further charge cannot create more copper than supplied.

criteria.criterion: Total deposited copper stays within the initial copper budget unless an explicitly modelled copper anode supplies more.
Identify the later cathodic product or an explicit refusal after Cu depletion.

cases.original_forecast: First-endpoint demand P should be near 0.7 mmol and total T near 1.0 mmol. Ideal reconstruction gives n(OH)=2P−T and n(CO3)=T−P.

criteria.criterion: The first endpoint accounts for more than half of total alkalinity.
The reconstructed hydroxide/carbonate quantities approximate 0.4/0.3 mmol.

cases.original_forecast: The stoichiometric requirement is 0.4 mmol permanganate, corresponding to 20 mL of the nominal 0.02 M titrant; a small persistent excess defines the endpoint.

criteria.criterion: Cumulative titrant volume brackets 20 mL with the chosen 0.2 mL step, subject to model response.
Inspect both oxalate depletion and persistent oxidant; a generic colour event is insufficient.

cases.original_forecast: A filter first passes dissolved nitrate solution; cooling the filtrate can produce crystals that a second filtration then retains.

criteria.criterion: Identify dissolved and solid KNO3 at both filtration steps.
Calculate crystal recovery from phase inventories, not from total vessel mass alone.
